## Finishing

Call submit_patch as your LAST action, after you have made and checked your
changes. Submitting ends your session: once the turn in which you call it
completes, the harness stops the task and you get no further turns. Do not
call it after your first edit and expect to keep working.

If you run out of time or tool calls without calling submit_patch, the harness
still collects your working-tree changes and scores them. So an edit you have
made is never lost — but an investigation you never turned into an edit is.

## Committing to an edit

By your 15th tool call you must have called edit_file or write_file on a file
under /workspace. If you have not, stop investigating and make your best edit
from what you have already read, even if you are unsure. Then keep working:
refine it, check it, and submit at the end.

An empty patch scores zero. A wrong patch also scores zero and costs you
nothing. Finishing without having edited a source file is the one outcome
that is always worse than guessing.

If a reproduction script fails to reproduce the issue twice, abandon it and
work from reading the code instead. Do not rewrite it a third time.

Call get_status to see your remaining time and tool calls. It is free and does
not count against your budget.

## Scratch files

Reproduction scripts go in /tmp, never inside /workspace — anything left in
/workspace becomes part of your patch. Do not modify test files, conftest.py
or pytest.ini; those changes are stripped before grading, so editing them
only wastes calls.

## Scope

Most fixes in these repositories touch ONE file and change fewer than ten
lines. Modify existing code rather than adding new code. Do not refactor,
reformat, or make unrelated changes. If your patch is growing past a few
files, stop and reconsider the diagnosis.

Exception: if the issue asks for functionality that does not exist yet,
create the file or function it describes, and match any names, CLI flags
or interfaces the issue specifies exactly.

## Finding the code

A truncated result loses information silently, so a broad read wastes a call
and leaves you guessing. Narrow before you read:

  run_command("grep -rln '<symbol>' --include='*.py' .")       # files only
  run_command("grep -n '<symbol>' path/to/one_file.py")        # then inside one

Use -l to find the file, then -n only within that file. Read with read_file on
a tight line range around the match. Never read a whole file and never cat
one — you will get an arbitrary prefix and burn the call.

from rich.console import Console
from rich.prompt import Prompt, InvalidResponse

class MyPrompt(Prompt):
    def process_response(self, value: str) -> str:
        if value != "yes":
            raise InvalidResponse("[red]Invalid response![/red]")
        return value

def test_markup_disabled():
    console = Console(markup=False)
    prompt = MyPrompt(console=console)
    
    # We want to see what happens when on_validate_error is called.
    # Since we can't easily simulate user input in a script without mocking,
    # we can call on_validate_error directly.
    
    error = InvalidResponse("[red]Invalid response![/red]")
    console.print("Before")
    prompt.on_validate_error("no", error)
    console.print("After")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_markup_disabled()

{"status": "ok", "filepath": "tests/test_prompt.py", "content": "import io

from rich.console import Console
from rich.prompt import Confirm, IntPrompt, Prompt


def test_prompt_str():
    INPUT = "egg\nfoo"
    console = Console(file=io.StringIO())
    name = Prompt.ask(
        "what is your name",
        console=console,
        choices=["foo", "bar"],
        default="baz",
        stream=io.StringIO(INPUT),
    )
    assert name == "foo"
    expected = "what is your name [foo/bar] (baz): Please select one of the available options\nwhat is your name [foo/bar] (baz): "
    output = console.file.getvalue()
    print(repr(output))
    assert output == expected


def test_prompt_str_case_insensitive():
    INPUT = "egg\nFoO"
    console = Console(file=io.StringIO())
    name = Prompt.ask(
        "what is your name",
        console=console,
        choices=["foo", "bar"],
        default="baz",
        case_sensitive=False,
        stream=io.StringIO(INPUT),
    )
    assert name == "foo"
    expected = "what is your name [foo/bar] (baz): Please select one of the available options\nwhat is your name [foo/bar] (baz): "
    output = console.file.getvalue()
    print(repr(output))
    assert output == expected


def test_prompt_str_default():
    INPUT = ""
    console = Console(file=io.StringIO())
    name = Prompt.ask(
        "what is your name",
        console=console,
        default="Will",
        stream=io.StringIO(INPUT),
    )
    assert name == "Will"
    expected = "what is your name (Will): "
    output = console.file.getvalue()
    print(repr(output))
    assert output == expected


def test_prompt_int():
    INPUT = "foo\n100"
    console = Console(file=io.StringIO())
    number = IntPrompt.ask(
        "Enter a number",
        console=console,
        stream=io.StringIO(INPUT),
    )
    assert number == 100
    expected = "Enter a number: Please enter a valid integer number\nEnter a number: "
    output = console.file.getvalue()
    print(repr(output))
    assert output == expected


def test_prompt_confirm_no():
    INPUT = "foo\nNO\nn"
    console = Console(file=io.StringIO())
    answer = Confirm.ask(
        "continue",
        console=console,
        stream=io.StringIO(INPUT),
    )
    assert answer is False
    expected = "continue [y/n]: Please enter Y or N\ncontinue [y/n]: Please enter Y or N\ncontinue [y/n]: "
    output = console.file.getvalue()
    print(repr(output))
    assert output == expected


def test_prompt_confirm_yes():
    INPUT = "foo\nNO\ny"
    console = Console(file=io.StringIO())
    answer = Confirm.ask(
        "continue",
        console=console,
        stream=io.StringIO(INPUT),
    )
    assert answer is True
    expected = "continue [y/n]: Please enter Y or N\ncontinue [y/n]: Please enter Y or N\ncontinue [y/n]: "
    output = console.file.getvalue()
    print(repr(output))
    assert output == expected


def test_prompt_confirm_default():
    INPUT = "foo\nNO\ny"
    console = Console(file=io.StringIO())
    answer = Confirm.ask(
        "continue", console=console, stream=io.StringIO(INPUT), default=True
    )
    assert answer is True
    expected = "continue [y/n] (y): Please enter Y or N\ncontinue [y/n] (y): Please enter Y or N\ncontinue [y/n] (y): "
    output = console.file.getvalue()
    print(repr(output))
    assert output == expected", "start_line": 1, "end_line": 113, "total_lines": 113, "is_truncated": false}

    from rich.prompt import Prompt, InvalidResponse

    class MyPrompt(Prompt):
        def process_response(self, value: str) -> str:
            if value != "yes":
                raise InvalidResponse("[red]Invalid response![/red]")
            return value

    INPUT = "no\nyes"
    console = Console(file=io.StringIO(), markup=False)
    result = MyPrompt.ask("continue", console=console, stream=io.StringIO(INPUT))
    assert result == "yes"
    output = console.file.getvalue()
    assert "Invalid response!" in output
    assert "[red]Invalid response![/red]" not in output
